question: How do a shared claim–abstract encoding and two distinct heads produce a label-conditioned returned rationale set without confusing input context, head inputs and decoding?

elements.role: One given claim plus title and all n≥1 abstract sentences; only abstract sentences are rationale candidates
One Longformer; global attention on <s>, all claim tokens and all </s> tokens
Contextual <s> to three-way label head; each sentence-final </s> to two-layer binary head and per-sentence two-way softmax
Predicted NEI empty; otherwise all scores strictly >0.5, or sole highest-scoring sentence only when that set is empty

logical decoding condition, not sentence-head input or computation schedule
strict threshold and conditional sole fallback

visual_design: Source Fig1 motivates context beyond highlighted evidence. Original A–C panels instead synthesize Methods: input identity, shared encoding with separate readouts, and explicit three-case decoding. Repeated symbols preserve pair/sentence identities; no source clinical text or fabricated scores.
transferable_rules: Identify what a condition changes: network input, loss, returned object or execution schedule. Do not convert output gating into a head-to-head feature edge.
Keep encoded context distinct from selected output membership. A fallback belongs to its full branch condition; preserve strict inequalities, all-versus-one cardinality and unresolved ties.
Native text proofs must cover ordinary spacing as well as formulas; font-derived visible-ink equivalence does not establish raw Unicode/contour identity.
